title: Statistical Sampling Profilers
description: Samples instruction pointers at 1 kHz to build hot-spot maps with under 2 percent overhead. Because sampling is statistical, it needs no instrumentation and works on production binaries. The profile shows where time really goes, not where developers guess it goes.
key_mechanisms: Sample the instruction pointer on a timer

demo.title: Demo — Statistical Sampling Profilers

title: eBPF Kernel Tracing
description: Attaches eBPF programs to kernel tracepoints for zero-instrumentation profiling. Safe bytecode runs in the kernel and aggregates data before sending it to userspace, so overhead stays tiny. It sees scheduling, I/O, and network events no userspace profiler can.

demo.title: Demo — eBPF Kernel Tracing

title: Flame Graph Rendering
description: Collapses stack samples into flame graphs for visual hotspot analysis. Each rectangle's width shows how much time a function was on-CPU, and stacks read top-down from caller to callee. Wide plateaus at the top are the optimization targets.

demo.title: Demo — Flame Graph Rendering

title: Allocation Profiling
description: Tracks malloc call sites to find allocation hot spots and churn. Programs rarely run out of memory — they churn through it, and allocation profiling shows which call sites create the most garbage. Cutting churn often beats tuning the collector.

demo.title: Demo — Allocation Profiling

title: Lock Contention Analysis
description: Measures futex wait times to find serialization bottlenecks. A lock held for microseconds but acquired millions of times serializes an otherwise parallel program. Contention profiles show which locks to split, shard, or eliminate.
key_mechanisms: Rank locks by total blocked time

demo.title: Demo — Lock Contention Analysis

title: I/O Wait Profiling
description: Attributes wall-clock time to block-layer waits versus compute. Off-CPU analysis shows threads stuck in disk or network waits that on-CPU profiles miss entirely. It answers whether the program is slow or just waiting.

demo.title: Demo — I/O Wait Profiling

title: GPU Kernel Profiling
description: Times CUDA kernels and memory copies to find GPU bottlenecks. Kernel timelines reveal whether the GPU is compute-bound, memory-bound, or starved by the host. Profiling also catches the classic bug: tiny kernels dominated by launch overhead.

demo.title: Demo — GPU Kernel Profiling

title: Continuous Profiling Agents
description: Runs always-on agents that stream profiles to central storage for fleet-wide analysis. Instead of profiling during incidents, every deploy's profile is already there, making regressions visible in diffs. Overhead stays under 1 percent so it can run everywhere.

demo.title: Demo — Continuous Profiling Agents

title: Anomaly Hotspot Detection
description: Flags functions whose profile share deviates from baseline using statistical change detection. A function jumping from 2 to 20 percent of CPU is an anomaly worth paging about. It turns profiles from a debugging tool into a monitoring signal.

demo.title: Demo — Anomaly Hotspot Detection

title: Energy Profiling
description: Correlates RAPL energy counters with code regions to find power hot spots. On battery-powered and dense datacenter machines, joules matter as much as seconds. Energy profiles guide optimizations that cut power without hurting speed.
key_mechanisms: Read RAPL energy counters per region

demo.title: Demo — Energy Profiling

title: Distributed Trace Aggregation
description: Merges spans across services into end-to-end latency breakdowns. A single request's journey through a dozen services becomes one waterfall showing exactly where time went. Aggregation also powers service dependency maps.

demo.title: Demo — Distributed Trace Aggregation

title: p99 Latency Attribution
description: Attributes tail latency to specific services and queries instead of averages that hide the pain. Users feel the tail, so the profiler ranks contributors to p99 and p999. Fixing the top tail contributor usually moves the whole percentile.

demo.title: Demo — p99 Latency Attribution

title: Cache-Miss Profiling
description: Uses hardware perf counters to map last-level-cache misses back to source lines. A single cache-thrashing line can dominate runtime, and only counters reveal it. The fix is usually layout: pack hot fields together and split hot from cold.
key_mechanisms: Sample LLC miss events with PEBS

demo.title: Demo — Cache-Miss Profiling

title: GC Pause Analysis
description: Logs garbage-collector pause distributions and their triggers to tame stop-the-world stalls. Pause histograms show whether the collector meets its goals; allocation profiles show why it runs so often. Tuning starts with measurement, not flags.
key_mechanisms: Log every GC pause with cause

demo.title: Demo — GC Pause Analysis

title: Profile-Guided Optimization Loops
description: Feeds production profiles back into the compiler automatically each release. The compiler uses real branch frequencies and hot paths to lay out code better than static heuristics can. Each release's profile trains the next release's binary.

demo.title: Demo — Profile-Guided Optimization Loops
